full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to this rule, in brief, are that the Sessions Judge received a telegram from Abdul Awal, opposite party No. 2 alleging that the petitioner acting as a Magistrate, 1st Class at Jhalakati in the presence of another Magistrate, and his lawyer Mr. Habib forcibly took his signatures on four white blank papers for the ostensible purpose of converting them into documents of amicable settlement of the dispute in a proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter called the Code) in M.R. Case No. 20 of 1978 pending in the Court of Sub-Divisional Magistrate Jhalakati. On receipt of the said telegram, the learned Sessions Judge started a criminal miscellaneous case and forwarded the telegram to the Sub- Divisional Magistrate, Jhalakati asking him to transmit the records of the case along with a report of the Magistrate concerned. On receipt of the records and the report of the Magistrate the learned Sessions Judge directed the complainant to appear in Court with his witnesses in support of his allegations. Thereafter; the petitioner filed an application before the Sessions Judge for an adjournment to move an application under section 526 of the Code before this Court. The learned Sessions Judge, however, rejected the prayer on the ground that section 526 of the Code was not applicable to the proceeding which was in the nature of preliminary inquiry. Thereafter the case was taken up for inquiry by the learned Sessions Judge and the statements of the complainant and his three witnesses were recorded. The petitioner then moved this Court and obtained the present rule and further proceedings in the matter were also stayed by this Court. We have heard Dr. Aleem-al-Razee in support of the rule; the learned Attorney General and Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman who appeared for the complainant opposite party No. 2 and opposed the rule.
